capabilities.operation: Host GameTime under a fixed time step
capabilities.evidence: CNA 0.21.0 issues one leading frame whose Update carries elapsed=0 and then reproduces pinned XNA Game.Tick exactly: Update sees ElapsedGameTime == TargetElapsedTime and the pre-increment TotalGameTime, Draw sees the advanced TotalGameTime. Pinned XNA returns from Tick without calling Update or DrawFrame when the accumulated/target step count is zero, so no XNA callback observes a zero elapsed time; the leading frame is an upstream divergence this binding reports rather than corrects. Pinned by NativeLifecycleTests.testHostGameTimeSequenceIsMeasuredNotAssumed; derivation in docs/native-abi-migration-evidence.md

cna_render_target2d_create succeeds on HEADLESS with renderer_available true; the granted kind, dimensions, level count, format, depth format, multisample count and usage are read back from cna_render_target_get_info; the same handle is accepted by cna_texture2d_get_info, cna_texture_get_info and cna_sprite_batch_submit_scaled_many, so the Texture2D substitutability is native rather than simulated; binding and restoring the backbuffer both succeed and destroying a bound target is refused with CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE. No pixel or visible output is claimed: the renderer is HEADLESS

a real cna_render_target_subscribe_content_lost registration is created and released, and a test asserts both. The event is never RAISED on this host: HEADLESS is one of the renderer families CNA documents as unable to lose a device, so IsContentLost is always false. XNA additionally latches the flag from GraphicsDevice.IsDeviceLost on every read, which has no counterpart here; the divergence is recorded in docs/foundation-38-derivability-and-render-target-evidence.md

capabilities.operation: Game timing, host state and the four host events
capabilities.evidence: Tick, SuppressDraw and ResetElapsedTime drive cna_game_tick, _suppress_draw and _reset_elapsed_time; IsActive, IsMouseVisible, IsFixedTimeStep, TargetElapsedTime and InactiveSleepTime are managed mirrors seeded from the host and moved only by a write the host accepted, because every one of those CLR getters is IL_NO_FAILURE_PATH and may not throw; Activated, Deactivated, Exiting and Disposed are four real cna_game_subscribe registrations, released at disposal

measured apart with a pure-C probe: CNA_GameCallbacks.exiting fires at cna_game_request_exit AND again at cna_game_destroy for a game that never ran, while CNA_GAME_EVENT_EXITING fires only at cna_game_request_exit. XNA raises Exiting when the game is exiting and raises nothing when a game that never ran is disposed, so the event is the mapped one and the lifecycle callback maps to nothing

GraphicsDeviceManager registers itself in Game.Services under both IGraphicsDeviceManager and IGraphicsDeviceService, refusing a second manager with the assembly's own GraphicsDeviceManagerAlreadyPresent message; its device comes from cna_graphics_device_manager_get_graphics_device and its four IGraphicsDeviceService events are real cna_graphics_device_manager_subscribe registrations. Game.GraphicsDevice and DrawableGameComponent resolve that service out of the container exactly as XNA does. Registering into the managed container creates no second lifecycle: CNA's native game owns the device and reads nothing from GameServiceContainer

capabilities.operation: Callback scope of a manager-supplied graphics device
capabilities.evidence: measured with a pure-C probe: cna_graphics_device_manager_get_graphics_device answers CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE with a zero handle before a game runs and after it exits, and succeeds with a real handle inside a lifecycle callback. The binding's own isInsideCallback guard is therefore defence in depth over a host that already refuses

All four types are complete managed Swift whose defaults and static presets are read out of the pinned XNA IL (SetDefaults and .cctor); ThrowIfBound reproduces the assembly's own BoundStateObject message. No device route is bound, so no state has yet been applied to a live CNA device and `isBound` is reachable only from within the module.

Reading a disposed RenderTarget2D inside a live LoadContent callback raises CNAObjectDisposedException with ObjectName 'RenderTarget2D', the composed message "Cannot access a disposed object.\r\nObject name: 'RenderTarget2D'." and HResult 0x80131622 — the class XNA's own Helpers.CheckDisposed raises, on the projected-exception channel rather than on CNAError. System.ObjectDisposedException is admitted as the seventh BCL exception authority out of mscorlib 5634668d…acc63.

Measured with a pure-C probe: cna_game_get_graphics_device answers a handle that is stable within one lifecycle callback and DIFFERENT in every callback — LoadContent, the first Update, the first Draw and the third Update each answer a distinct value, and a second run continues the sequence. The handle is therefore a per-callback capability token and not the device's identity, so XNA's device-owned managed state (cachedBlendState and the sampler collections, which live as long as the device) cannot be anchored to the callback-scoped facade. No device-state member is projected yet; when one is, its storage must be anchored to the game, which is the object with the device's lifetime.

XNA's pinned IL declares BlendFunction.Min = 3 and Max = 4; CNA's graphics_state.h declares CNA_BLEND_FUNCTION_MAX = 3 and MIN = 4. The two are swapped, so a rawValue pass-through would silently exchange them. Every other state enum — Blend, ColorWriteChannels, CompareFunction, StencilOperation, CullMode, FillMode, TextureAddressMode and TextureFilter — agrees value for value. No state route is bound yet; when one is, the conversion must be an exhaustive explicit map for every enum rather than a raw cast.

Complete managed Swift. The type-size table, the maximum-end-offset stride rule, the five validation failures and the order they are checked in all come from the pinned VertexElementValidator IL. CNA's own cna_vertex_declaration_create computes the same stride for four layouts chosen to separate a sum from a maximum and an ordered scan from an unordered one (build-probe/f43_stride.c) — corroboration, not authority. No cna_vertex_declaration_* route is bound, because no projected member consumes a declaration yet.

capabilities.operation: IVertexType and the four vertex structs
capabilities.evidence: All five are complete managed Swift. The four static VertexDeclaration fields are built by the same one-argument constructor XNA's class constructors use, so their strides (16/24/32/20) are computed by Foundation 43's rule rather than transcribed. The limitation is the Swift 6.0.3 toolchain, not the projection: opening an `any Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.IVertexType` existential and reading its property crashes swift-frontend in IR generation with "Forming a CanType out of a non-canonical type!". Concrete access, the static field and a generic constraint all compile, and `any IGraphicsDeviceService` and `any IPackedVector` open fine, so it is neither existentials in general nor this binding's nested namespaces. A consumer on this toolchain must use a generic constraint.
